newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: ARBED ELECTRIC OVEN TO TEST FROM MAY.
newsitem.headline: ARBED ELECTRIC OVEN TO TEST FROM MAY.

text.p: Luxembourg steel maker Arbed said on Wednesday the first trials of its fourth electric arc furnace would take place in May or June this year, with the blast furnace it replaces closing down in the middle of 1997.
"There will an overlap of about two months. We are within the programme, and there are no foreseeable difficulties," Arbed's president Joseph Kinsch told Reuters in an interview.

When the new furnace at its Esch-Belval site in Luxembourg is operational, Arbed will have completed its transition to the more efficient and adaptable electric steel-making process in its long products sector. A continuous caster is also being built at the complex.

In its 1996 annual report, published last June, the group said cost prices in the long products sector had been put under a temporary handicap during 1995 because of the simultaneous operation of two production processes during the switch over to electric furnaces.
Kinsch said cost benefits of the fourth electric furnace should show through in 1998.
He saw no problems in the long term with the supply of scrap, which the electric furnaces use instead of iron ore to make steel.
"The availability of scrap will not pose any problem for the future here in our region (which) is today a net exporter of scrap," he said.
